routes.label: Evaluate at two positive rational inputs

question:
If

\[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{a}{10^x-1}+\frac{b}{10^x+2}\\ &\qquad=\frac{2\cdot10^x+3} {(10^x-1)(10^x+2)} \end{aligned} \]

is an identity for positive rational values of \(x,\) then the value of \(a-b\) is:
solution:
An identity holds at every permitted input, so choosing two positive rational values of \(x\) gives two equations for the constants \(a\) and \(b\). Since \(x>0\), we have \(10^x>1\), so both denominators are nonzero. Clearing them gives
\[
a(10^x+2)+b(10^x-1)=2\cdot10^x+3.
\]
Taking \(x=1\) and \(x=2\), respectively, gives
\[
12a+9b=23,
\qquad 102a+99b=203.
\]
Subtracting the first equation from the second yields \(90a+90b=180\), so \(a+b=2\). The first equation can now be written as
\[
9(a+b)+3a=23,
\]
which gives \(18+3a=23\). Thus \(a=5/3\) and \(b=1/3\).

These values satisfy the entire identity, not merely the two selected inputs: writing \(t=10^x\), their combined numerator is
\[
\frac53(t+2)+\frac13(t-1)=2t+3.
\]
Therefore \(a-b=\frac43\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The repeated expression \(10^x\) can be treated as one quantity. Put \(t=10^x\). Since \(x>0\), we have \(t>1\), so the common denominator \((t-1)(t+2)\) is nonzero. Combining the fractions gives
\[
\frac{(a+b)t+2a-b}{(t-1)(t+2)}
=
\frac{2t+3}{(t-1)(t+2)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
(a+b-2)t+(2a-b-3)=0
\]
for every allowed \(t\). A nonzero linear expression can vanish at at most one value, while \(x=1\) and \(x=2\) already give two different values of \(t\). Both coefficients must therefore be zero:
\[
a+b=2,
\qquad 2a-b=3.
\]
Adding these equations gives \(3a=5\), so \(a=5/3\) and \(b=1/3\). These values make the two numerators identical, verifying the original identity throughout its stated domain. Hence \(a-b=\frac43\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Compare the numerator coefficients

edges.reason: This target explicitly asks for the justification of transposition, which is applying the same addition/subtraction to both sides.
After eliminating one unknown the procedure solves a one-variable linear equation; only this solving component is claimed.
Substitution seeks a pair satisfying both equations, so system and common-solution meanings are essential.
Substitution introduces the reduction-to-one-variable idea, but adding equations to cancel an unknown is justified independently by equality operations.
The reduction and back-substitution leave one-variable linear equations that must be solved; this is not a claim that every route must name transposition.
Adding/subtracting equations is performed to find their common solutions, not unrelated separate equation values.
